title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
body:
**Summary**

File uploads under ~10KB hang indefinitely (eventually timing out client-side) when `sentry_sdk.init()` is called in the same process, before Streamlit's own event loop is created, and Streamlit is then started in that process (e.g. via `streamlit.web.cli.main()` after rewriting `sys.argv`, rather than a fresh `streamlit run` subprocess). Uploads over ~10KB are unaffected. This reproduces with no application code beyond a single `st.file_uploader()`.

This in-process launch pattern is common for wrapper entrypoints that do setup (init error tracking, run DB migrations, etc.) before starting Streamlit without spawning a new OS process.

**Reproducible Code Example**

```python
"""
pip install streamlit==1.61.1 sentry-sdk==2.61.1
python repro.py
Then open http://localhost:8501 and upload a file smaller than ~10KB.
"""
import sys
import pathlib

pathlib.Path("app.py").write_text('''
import streamlit as st
uploaded = st.file_uploader("pick a file")
if uploaded is not None:
    st.write(f"Got {uploaded.name}, {len(uploaded.getvalue())} bytes")
''')

import sentry_sdk
sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None)  # comment this line out and the hang disappears

from streamlit.web import cli
sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", "app.py"]
sys.exit(cli.main())
```

**Steps To Reproduce**

1. `pip install streamlit==1.61.1 sentry-sdk==2.61.1`
2. Save the snippet above as `repro.py`, run `python repro.py`
3. Open `http://localhost:8501`, upload any file smaller than ~10KB (e.g. a 300-byte CSV)
4. Upload hangs indefinitely. Comment out `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None)` and it succeeds instantly. Upload a file larger than ~10KB and it succeeds either way.

**Expected Behavior**

Upload completes regardless of file size or whether Sentry was initialized in-process before Streamlit started.

**Current Behavior**

Small uploads hang. Root-caused to Sentry's `StarletteIntegration` (enabled by default) — confirmed via `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None, disabled_integrations=[StarletteIntegration()])` (succeeds) vs. `disabled_integrations=[ThreadingIntegration()]` (still hangs — ruling out threading despite superficial similarity to #15374 / #16139, both of which are already fixed in this version and don't apply since this repro has no `st.fragment(run_every=...)`). `StarletteIntegration` instruments Starlette's ASGI request lifecycle, and the hang lives inside Starlette's own multipart parser — Sentry wraps exactly the layer that breaks.

**Is this a regression?**

Not tested on older versions — can test if useful.

**Debug info**

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: macOS (also reproduces in a Linux container)
- sentry-sdk version: 2.61.1

**Additional Information**

Fuller repro with isolation scripts (control, all-integrations-disabled, Starlette-only-disabled) and sample CSVs: https://gist.github.com/tbrambor/d41b40950a0061ca404fc0d67e4768ed

comments.body:
Found the precise mechanism, which also explains the exact ~10KB boundary — filed against sentry-python since it's really their code path: https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/7285

In short: `StarletteIntegration.patch_request_response()` wraps every route endpoint (including `_upload_put`). Before the handler runs, Sentry's `StarletteRequestExtractor.extract_request_info()` calls `await request.body()`/`.form()` whenever `content_length` is within its default `max_request_body_size` ("medium" → `content_length <= 10_000` bytes) — this fully drains the ASGI `receive()` channel purely to populate breadcrumb/event data.

`_upload_put` (`streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py`) then builds its own `StarletteRequest(request.scope, limited_receive)` to enforce a streaming size cap, where `limited_receive` calls `await request.receive()` directly — the same raw ASGI channel Sentry already drained. That second read blocks forever (no more body left, no disconnect coming on a keep-alive connection), which is the hang.

For uploads over 10,000 bytes, Sentry's size check skips body capture entirely, so the channel is untouched and the upload succeeds — matching the exact size boundary seen in testing.

This isn't really fixable from Streamlit's side alone — any ASGI middleware that reads the body first (not just Sentry) would break `_upload_put`'s manual receive the same way, since it isn't going through Starlette's own cached `Request.body()`/`.stream()`. Flagging here for visibility in case a defensive fix on this side (e.g. checking whether the body was already consumed, or reusing the original request via `Request.stream()`/cached body when available) is worth considering regardless of how the Sentry side lands.

`st.file_uploader` hangs on uploads under ~10KB when `sentry_sdk.init()` runs in the same process before Streamlit starts. Sentry’s default `StarletteIntegration` drains the ASGI body (via `request.body()` / `.form()`) for requests with `content_length <= 10_000`. `_upload_put` in `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py` then wraps `request.receive()` in `limited_receive` and builds a **new** `StarletteRequest` for multipart parsing, which does not see Starlette’s cached body. The second `receive()` blocks indefinitely on a keep-alive connection. Uploads over ~10KB skip Sentry body capture, matching the reported boundary. The same `/_stcore/upload_file` route is used by `st.camera_input` and `st.chat_input` attachments. Workaround: disable `StarletteIntegration` (or avoid in-process Sentry init). A Streamlit-side defensive fix would reuse the original request’s cached body / `Request.stream()` instead of a raw second `receive()`.

### Related Issues

- [#16139](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16139) — Closed. Another in-process `sentry_sdk.init()` interaction with Streamlit (ThreadingIntegration + `st.fragment(run_every)`). Different mechanism; the reporter correctly ruled this out.
- [#15374](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15374) — Closed. Sentry/threading wrapper clash around `add_script_run_ctx` in 1.58.0. Same “Sentry instruments Streamlit in-process” class of bug, not a duplicate of this hang.
- Upstream: [getsentry/sentry-python#7285](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/7285) — Reporter’s Sentry-side write-up of the body-drain + second `receive()` hang.

No open Streamlit duplicates found. Other `st.file_uploader` timeout issues (e.g. [#11419](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11419)) are unrelated client/mobile timeouts.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `cursor-grok-4.6-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

Confirmed, and your root-cause analysis is exactly right — thank you, the write-up made this quick to verify. Editing this comment to keep everything in one place now that we've implemented a fix; the mechanism section is unchanged, the "which middleware patterns break" characterization is corrected, and the open question about Sentry's `Request` instance is resolved.

**Mechanism**

Confirmed against Starlette 1.6.0: `Request.body()` caches into `self._body` **per instance**, and `stream()` only consults `hasattr(self, "_body")`. Because `_upload_put` constructs a *new* `StarletteRequest(request.scope, limited_receive)` whose `limited_receive` calls the raw `request.receive()`, it can never see that cache. The second read then blocks forever on a keep-alive connection. Reproduced with no `sentry_sdk` installed at all, using a stand-in that reads the request body before the handler runs:

```
CASE 1: no middleware reading the body (control)
  RESULT: completed, status=204
CASE 2: middleware reads body first (models Sentry StarletteIntegration)
  middleware pre-read 159 bytes of body
  RESULT: *** HUNG *** (timed out after 3s; receive() called 2x)
```

**It's a regression in 1.61.0**

You mentioned you hadn't tested older versions, so: the `limited_receive` pattern was introduced in #16207 ("Enforce upload size limit while streaming body"), which shipped in **1.61.0**. Before that, the handler called `await request.form()` on the *original* request, which is cache-aware. Same drained-channel scenario against the old code path:

```
OLD (pre-#16207) `await request.form()`: OK -> ['foo.txt']  (receive calls: 1)
```

So 1.60.x and earlier are unaffected, and 1.61.0 onward is broken.

**Which patterns actually break (correcting an earlier overstatement)**

An earlier version of this comment said `_upload_put` is incompatible with *any* body-reading ASGI middleware. That was too broad. Measured against a real uvicorn server with keep-alive, there are three distinct patterns, and only some break:

| Pattern | Before fix | After fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No middleware | 204 | 204 |
| Reads the body via the **same** `Request` the endpoint receives (Sentry's `StarletteIntegration`, which patches `starlette.routing.request_response`) | **hangs** | 204 |
| Buffers the body and replays it downstream (the well-behaved ASGI contract) | 204 | 204 |
| Consumes the raw channel and passes it down **without** replaying | **hangs** | **still hangs** |

The last row is not recoverable from our side — the bytes are genuinely gone, and the handler can't distinguish "no more body coming" from "body still in flight" without a disconnect. Worth flagging for anyone wrapping Streamlit in a custom ASGI stack: buffer-and-replay is safe, drain-without-replay is not, and that holds independently of this fix.

**Your open question, resolved**

Sentry does read from the same `Request` instance, so a cache-aware read is sufficient and no buffering workaround is needed. In `sentry_sdk.integrations.starlette`, `_wrap_async_handler` does `request = args[0]` and then `StarletteRequestExtractor(request)`; the extractor's `form()` deliberately calls `await self.request.body()` first (with a comment noting Starlette doesn't cache `form()` the way it caches `body()`). Verified against sentry-sdk 2.68.1. The ~10KB boundary is `request_body_within_bounds` under the default `max_request_body_size="medium"`, matching your numbers exactly.

**The fix**

`_upload_put` now reads through the original request's `stream()` — which replays Starlette's cached body when present — instead of the raw `receive()` channel, while still counting bytes to preserve #16207's streaming size cap. That cap exists to stop an oversized upload from being buffered in memory or spooled to disk before the size check runs, so we didn't want to trade this hang for that. Verified end to end against real sentry-sdk 2.68.1 + uvicorn: the sub-10KB upload that previously hung now returns 204, and the >10KB case is unchanged.

One behavior change worth noting: a body consumed without being cached now returns a clear 400 rather than hanging or surfacing an opaque 500.

**Triage**

Confirmed bug, prioritized as a regression affecting `st.file_uploader`, `st.chat_input` attachments, `st.camera_input`, and `st.audio_input` — all four share the `/_stcore/upload_file` route. The silent-hang failure mode with no error or log makes this disproportionately hard to diagnose, which we weighted in.

Thanks also for filing [getsentry/sentry-python#7285](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/7285). We're fixing this on our side regardless, since that upstream fix would address one trigger rather than the pattern.

In the meantime, for anyone hitting this on 1.61.x: `disabled_integrations=[StarletteIntegration()]` in your `sentry_sdk.init()` avoids it, at the cost of Sentry's Starlette request instrumentation.
